title: Byzantine-Robust and Differentially Private Federated Optimization under Weaker Assumptions

C-a.quote: It is crucial to bound model updates before injecting DP-noise. Without clipping, updates may have arbitrarily large norms, which would dominate the injected noise and invalidate the privacy guarantee. Clipping restricts each update to a controlled range, ensuring that the privacy guarantees remain meaningful and that the added noise achieves its intended effect. In Byz-Clip21-SGD2M, we employ the standard norm-clipping mechanism, which rescales updates relative to a threshold τ :   τ x, if ∥x∥> τ, clipτ (x) = ∥x∥ (8) x, if ∥x∥≤ τ. This procedure ensures a fixed sensitivity at each update, after which Gaussian noise is added to the clipped values to provide local (ε, δ)-DP guarantees.
C-a.locator: §4 Algorithm Design; THE CLIPPING STAGE'S STATED PURPOSE IS PRIVACY, NOT RESISTING POISONED UPDATES, so Amendment 3 excises it, and the paper confirms the reading by saying what happens when privacy is switched off: "In this regime, clipping, originally required for privacy guarantees, is no longer needed." (§5). ONLY ONE COMPONENT CARRIES A DEFENSE PURPOSE: the robust aggregation rule, "To mitigate adversarial clients that attempt to disrupt training, we employ a robust aggregation rule satisfying Definition 3.2." (§3), the mechanism "At the heart of robust Byz-Clip21-SGD2M lies the aggregation rule RAgg." (§4), defined at "The aggregation rule RAgg is said to be (δbyz , c)-robust if" (Definition 3.2). ALSO EXCLUDED, with its own purpose quotations: the DOUBLE MOMENTUM, whose stated job is noise and variance control for convergence, "Byz-Clip21-SGD2M employs two momentum buffers, {vit }i∈G on the client side and {mti }i∈G on the server side, both essential for mitigating noise during training." (§4) and "On the client side, momentum with parameter β smooths mini-batch gradient noise; without it, the method may fail to converge" (§4), and whose server-side buffer is given a heterogeneity purpose, "Incorporating this mechanism into Byz-Clip21-SGD2M allows the algorithm to compensate for the bias introduced by heterogeneous client data, thereby ensuring convergence under larger levels of data heterogeneity." (§4); the momentum's interaction with clipping is likewise stated in convergence terms, "In our setting, the updates ct+1 are used to update the momenta mt+1 i i , which are then aggregated through RAgg. The stability of mt+1 is maintained by the clipping operator, since without such i control the norm could otherwise grow unbounded. Moreover, due to our design choice β̂ ∼ 1/T , the growth rate of the norm is limited to O(tτ β̂) = O(1), ensuring that the momenta remain well-behaved throughout the training process." (Remark 5.1). The composition is therefore ONE defense mechanism plus a privacy mechanism plus a variance-reduction mechanism, which is the DDFed and CQSA class shape, and C-a cannot reach two.

C-b.quote: These vulnerabilities highlight the need to address differential privacy (DP) and Byzantine robustness within a unified framework.
C-b.locator: Abstract; the pairing reason the paper gives is threat coverage -- gradient leakage on one side, Byzantine manipulation on the other -- but it pairs the ONE counted defense mechanism with the EXCISED privacy mechanism, so it is not a reason for pairing two counted constituents. This is the fifth instance of Amendment 3's excised-constituent limit (after 2601.04930, 2601.06466, 2602.22269 and 2603.04422). The only other constituent-property reason in the paper is a convergence reason for pairing momentum with clipping, "On the client side, momentum with parameter β smooths mini-batch gradient noise; without it, the method may fail to converge" (§4), and both of those are excised. No quotation gives a reason turning on the robust aggregator's standalone effectiveness or on complementary coverage between two counted defenses.

C-d.locator: Figures 1-2; WITHIN A PANEL the privacy budget is swept over five reported settings while the attack is held fixed -- the panel labels fix the adversary population and the attack, "Final Test Accuracy 70 60 50 40 30 20 10 Final Test Accuracy 80 70 60 50 40 30 20 Byz-Clip-SGD Safe-DSHB Byz-Clip21-SGD2M 3 8 13 18 23 Privacy Budget " ^ CNN, 2 Byzantine Clients", and the x-axis carries epsilon at 3, 8, 13, 18, 23 -- and the downstream robust aggregation rule is unchanged across the sweep. This is the DDFed shape: the varied upstream stage is the PRIVACY perturbation, which Amendment 3 excludes from C-a, and C-d's frozen text does not require the varied stage to be a defense. The hyperparameter route's reported-results floor is cleared five times over. AN ANALYTIC ROUTE IS ALSO PRESENT AND IS STRONGER THAN THE SWEEP: Theorem 5.1's utility bound is written as a function of the DP-noise variance and the (c, delta_byz)-robust aggregator's constants jointly, and the paper reads the interaction off it -- "We observe that the first term is purely due to DP noise, the middle term is a mix of DP noise and robust aggregation, and the last term is purely due to robust aggregation." (App. D) and "In Corollary 5.1, the first term corresponds to the error arising from privacy, while the last term reflects the error introduced by the presence of Byzantine clients. The middle term represents the additional penalty incurred when enforcing both requirements simultaneously." (§5). The code does not depend on which route is taken.

C-e.quote: In Corollary 5.1, the first term corresponds to the error arising from privacy, while the last term reflects the error introduced by the presence of Byzantine clients. The middle term represents the additional penalty incurred when enforcing both requirements simultaneously.
C-e.locator: §5, following Corollary 5.1; the claim decomposes the composed system's error into a part attributable to each constituent plus a part attributable to their INTERACTION, and the paper states the sign and form of that interaction: "Theorem 5.1 shows that the impacts of privacy and Byzantine adversaries multiply." (§5). The mechanism reason for the interaction is given in the introduction, "using robust aggregation to combine the DP-noisy updates can amplify the detrimental effects of noise, further hindering convergence." (§1), and the momentum's contribution is attributed separately in Remark 5.1's discussion.

coder_note:
THIS ROW IS THE AUDIT'S MOST VALUABLE EXTERNAL ANCHOR AND IT IS NOT A PRIMARY. It is a theory paper with 33 theorems and 60 lemmas, and it PROVES that composing a privacy mechanism with a robust aggregator produces an error term belonging to neither constituent: "the middle term represents the additional penalty incurred when enforcing both requirements simultaneously", summarised as "Theorem 5.1 shows that the impacts of privacy and Byzantine adversaries multiply". The mechanism is stated in the introduction: "using robust aggregation to combine the DP-noisy updates can amplify the detrimental effects of noise, further hindering convergence". That is a proof, in the external literature, that a composed defense's behaviour does not decompose into its constituents' -- the exact proposition main.tex argues for, arrived at independently and by analysis rather than measurement.

IT IS THE FIFTH EXTERNAL TREATMENT OF COMPOSITION INTERACTION AND THE FIRST WITH THE OPPOSITE SIGN, WHICH IS WHY A3 SHOULD LEAD WITH THE SET RATHER THAN WITH A RATE. Fed-DPRoC PROVES a guarantee survives an upstream transform; SRFed Thm 6.2 PROVES a detector's decisions are unchanged by an upstream perturbation; CQSA PROVES the downstream statistic is preserved and then declines to measure; DDFed MEASURES a detector's effectiveness across upstream noise and finds no effect. All four report invariance. This paper proves a multiplicative PENALTY. So the external literature contains both answers to the composition question, obtained by four proofs and one measurement, and no paper in the frame measures the interaction it claims -- which is a sharper and more defensible statement of the gap than any prevalence figure, and it is the form A3 and A4 should take.

C-a = NO ON ONE COUNTED COMPONENT, AND THIS ROW NAMES A CLASS THE FRAME NOW HAS SEVERAL MEMBERS OF: papers that pass the screen (two or more mechanisms genuinely applied together in one round) and fail C-a (only one of them is defense-purposed under Amendment 3). Here the three stages are robust aggregation (defense), clipping (privacy: "It is crucial to bound model updates before injecting DP-noise", and the paper itself says clipping is dispensable once privacy is dropped), and double momentum (variance reduction and heterogeneity bias correction, stated in convergence terms). A5 should report the count of such rows, because it is the honest answer to a reader who objects that C-a's threshold is doing the work: the screen and the criterion measure different things on purpose, and the rows where they disagree are visible.

C-b = NO IS THE FIFTH EXCISED-CONSTITUENT INSTANCE AND THE CLEANEST ILLUSTRATION OF THE COST. The paper's pairing reason is complementary threat coverage stated in one sentence in the abstract -- leakage and Byzantine manipulation are different threats and the framework addresses both -- which is precisely the reasoning C-b was written to detect. It is unusable because one of the two constituents is excised as privacy-purposed. Five instances now, with excised purposes spanning privacy, cryptography, fairness, communication and heterogeneity, so A5's recommendation should be stated as a finding rather than a suggestion: a per-component purpose test cannot see a criterion that is about a RELATION between components, and the audit's C-b rate is therefore a lower bound on how often papers give constituent-property reasons.

C-d = YES ON TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES, AND THE ANALYTIC ONE IS THE BETTER MEASUREMENT. The empirical sweep is the DDFed shape and clears the reported-results floor: five privacy budgets, adversary count and attack fixed within each panel, downstream aggregator unchanged. The analytic route is stronger, because the bound is a function of the upstream noise variance and the downstream aggregator's robustness constants jointly, so it identifies the dependence rather than sampling it at five points. Recording both matters for A4: this is a paper that ran the identifying contrast in the strongest form available to it, so it is a second exhibit alongside SpectralKrum and SRFed against any implication that nobody runs the contrast.

EXTRACTOR NOT USED FOR THIS ROW. At 162187 characters, with 100 occurrences of Byzantine and 66 of clip, every coded quotation came from targeted sentence-level greps on the component-purpose vocabulary and from reading §4, §5 and §6. The aid's C-c and C-d buckets were not consulted, so this row contributes no data point to the bucket-performance tallies; A5 should say so rather than let the denominators drift.

DATA-QUALITY NOTE: MNIST only, CNN and MLP, IPM attack, and the figures report no error bars or seed counts. That is thin for an empirical claim and generous for a theory paper, and it does not affect any code here. Retained under non-negotiable 7.
